data.title: Middle East Eye: ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide could strengthen South Africa's case against Israel
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide could strengthen South Africa's case against Israel
The International Court of Justice's landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya could have far-reaching consequences for Israel, after judges rejected the argument that military operations against armed groups provided an adequate explanation for a campaign of mass killings, sexual violence and widespread destruction.
The judgment, the first time the UN's highest court has found a state responsible for genocide, offers South Africa a potentially significant legal precedent in its case accusing Israel of committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, particularly over how judges assess genocidal intent when a state claims its military actions are driven by security objectives.
In a 9-6 decision on Thursday, the ICJ found that Myanmar's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya population in northern Rakhine State during the military's 2017 operations.
"The only reasonable inference that can explain Myanmar's actions is an intention to destroy a substantial part of the protected group, namely the Rohingya population in Northern Rakhine State," the court said.
The judgment is particularly significant for South Africa's case, which hinges on establishing that Israel acted with the specific intention of destroying Palestinians, in whole or in part, as a national, ethnic, racial or religious group.
Read more: ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide could strengthen South Africa's case against Israel

data.title: Middle East Eye: UK trade envoy to Israel backs troll account which attacked Ed Miliband and Labour over Muslims
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
UK trade envoy to Israel backs troll account which attacked Ed Miliband and Labour over Muslims
The UK's trade envoy to Israel has endorsed a social media account which has disparagingly labelled the foreign secretary the "Palestine secretary" and repeatedly attacked the Labour government, claiming it is trying to appease Muslims.
Earlier this week Byline Times reported that @habibi_uk, the anonymous account on X which campaigns against pro-Palestine public figures in the UK, is the American-British grandson of the philosopher Bertrand Russell and a US State Department-trained expert in "political-military diplomacy" called Benjamin Tait.
Tait has previously worked with Lord Ian Austin, a former Labour MP and life peer who has been the trade envoy to Israel under successive governments since July 2019.
Austin posted on X on Wednesday, in response to the Habibi account: "Keep going", followed by two emojis of a muscled arm and two clapping emojis.
Habibi has labelled British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband the "Palestine Secretary", commenting last month: "Oh look, the Palestine Secretary is hard at work."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Somalia expels Emirati envoy, recalls own ambassador over 'open invasion'
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Somalia expels Emirati envoy, recalls own ambassador over 'open invasion'
Somalia has ordered the UAE ambassador to leave the country within 72 hours, and recalled his Somali counterpart from Abu Dhabi, citing an "open invasion" against "the sovereignty, security, land and unity of the Somalis".
Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud announced the decision at a news conference in the Somali capital Mogadishu, warning that "measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with the UAE in the invasion against Somalia".
“All Somalis are urged to defend their country and unite against the open invasion of the UAE against the sovereignty, security, land and unity of Somalis,” Mohamud said, without elaborating on what provoked the expulsion.
There was no immediate response from the Emirati foreign ministry, but Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, condemned the comments in a post on X as an “attack”, which he said “reflects the shifting nature of his positions and policies, and raises questions about his prioritisation of personal calculations over his country’s national interests”.
Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on Tuesday accused the UAE of "interference" in his country's internal affairs, and alleged that Abu Dhabi was backing armed groups and fuelling divisions between the federal government and regional administrations.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UK school pays compensation to children threatened over Palestinian badges
data.author: Areeb Ullah
data.summary:
UK school pays compensation to children threatened over Palestinian badges
Submitted by
Areeb Ullah
on
Thu, 11/19/2026 - 16:12
Lion Academy Trust threatened to refer children to Prevent for wearing colours in memory of children killed in Gaza
Hundreds of parents and supporters staged a protest outside Barclay primary school in east London after the Lion Academy Trust did not respond to a parent letter (Supplied)
Off
A UK school trust has apologised and agreed to pay compensation to four children who were threatened with referrals to the government’s counterterrorism Prevent programme after wearing Palestinian colours and badges at a school charity event.
The children attended Barclay Primary School in Leyton, east London, in November 2023, when they wore Palestinian colours in memory of children killed in Gaza during the school’s Children in Need event.
The primary school is part of the Lion Academy Trust, which runs 11 primary academies in east London.
Following the event, the children's parents received letters warning that they could be referred to Prevent or to the police’s hate crime unit for wearing the Palestine flag or its colours, which it deemed “overt demonstrations of political beliefs” that could be “deemed offensive".
Middle East Eye understands that the letter was sent to the families of a number of children, including an eight-year-old who lost 14 members of his family in Gaza.
Prevent Watch, which has supported the families throughout its three-year legal battle, confirmed to MEE that a court approved the settlement on Thursday after the families, represented by law firm Leigh Day, brought claims under the Equality Act 2010 and the Human Rights Act 1998.
The case has renewed concerns about the use of the UK’s counterterrorism framework in educational settings and the treatment of Palestinian solidarity in schools.
The Lion Academy Trust did not respond to MEE's request for comment at the time of publication.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund skyscraper
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund skyscraper
The skyscraper housing Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) in Riyadh was damaged on Thursday by a Houthi strike, the kingdom has confirmed.
The strike destroyed windows across seven to eight floors of the tower, Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, and bent part of its metal facade, according to a Reuters journalist. Video footage shared from the Saudi capital showed crews already working to replace the glass.
The attack is the second time this month that the Houthis have struck at the heart of Saudi Arabia’s image as a safe investment destination. PIF says it has around $1 trillion in assets. Earlier this month, the Houthis struck Aramco Tower in Riyadh.
“One of the towers of the Financial Center in Riyadh was targeted in a terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia, causing material damage but no injuries -praise be to God,” the Saudi authorities said in a statement released on Thursday.
The press release included an image showing notable but relatively minor damage to the PIF headquarters. Video footage appeared to show a missile slamming into the 80-storey tower, but Middle East Eye could not independently verify the footage.

UN chief defends ICC after Russian, US, Chinese criticism
United Nations chief Antonio Guterres hailed the "crucial" role of the International Criminal Court (ICC) after it faced criticism from the US, Russia and China.
"The Secretary-General believes that the International Criminal Court is one of the crucial bodies for international justice in the world," Guterres's spokesperson Farhan Haq said on Thursday.
"We want its work to be supported by member states. The pillar of the rule of law is one of the founding pillars of of the stability of the world, and it must be reinforced and not weakened," he added.
The ICC has issued arrest warrants for senior officials in Russia and Israel, and is investigating both countries for war crimes.

Qatar’s foreign ministry also strongly condemned what it described as "a disgraceful act of aggression, an unacceptable disregard for civilian lives, a blatant violation of Saudi Arabia's sovereignty, and a clear breach of the principles of international law" in a statement posted on X.

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves

Iran’s navy says oil tanker struck naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz
Iran’s navy said on Thursday that an oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's IRIB.
The “offending” tanker “had switched off its navigation systems”, IRIB reported the Iranian navy as saying in a statement.

data.title: Middle East Eye: At least 300 children died in Gaza waiting for Israel's permission to get medical leave
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
At least 300 children died in Gaza waiting for Israel's permission to get medical leave
Gaza’s health ministry said on Thursday that at least 300 children have died awaiting Israel's permission to leave for life-saving medical treatment, including at least 90 children suffering from cancer.
Another 5,400 children are still on medical travel lists, waiting to secure Israeli authorisation to leave the enclave, health officials added.
In February, the ministry reported that 1,360 patients in Gaza died while waiting for medical travel permits after the Rafah crossing was closed in May 2024.
